45ad079ccecf8e8b5824f88b4194c958e3f977c5.rationale: Immunohistochemical staining and skin punch biopsy results are consistent with Mycosis Fungoides

Mycosis fungoides: Previous treatments: multiple courses of oral prednisolone and cyclosporine
Response to previous treatments: no improvement
CD30 positive in fewer than 25% of lymphocytes
Initial symptoms: slightly pruritic, slowly progressive erythematous lesions on trunk and retroauricular area
Examination findings: confluent lichenified erythromelanotic plaques with overlying thick greasy scales on face, neck, trunk, genitalia, upper and lower extremities, palms, and soles
Skin punch biopsies: epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes and superficial dermal band‐like lymphocytic infiltrate with dermal fibrosis
Immunohistochemical staining: tumor cells positive for CD3 and CD45RO, negative for CD4, CD8, and CD7
